title: Binary classification
description: A yes or no for each row: churn, default, acceptance.
metrics: Recall at the review budget (the share of cases found when the team reviews its budget)
question: Which decisions does DCLab reach on a binary classification problem (A yes or no for each row: churn, default, acceptance), and do they hold?
hypothesis: Each decision a careful data scientist reaches on this kind of problem holds on every seed of the kind's replica.
setup_summary: The binary classification kind's replica on seeds 0, 1, 2, brought as a person would; the five stages of the engine solve it, and each decision is checked on the finished run. No model is called.

decisions.decision: `final_refund_amount` is kept out of the model (paid only after a cancellation)
`subscriber_id` is kept out of the model (an identifier)
the holdout is the latest signups
scored by ROC-AUC (cancellations are not rare)
the leakage audit measures how much the refund would have inflated the score (by more than 0.1)
the holdout ROC-AUC is at least 0.65 and 0.1 above chance
the baselines the kind declares are the ones the final stage computes

claims.statement: Binary classification: on 3 of 3 seeds every decision held (95% interval over seeds [0.439, 1.0]); 21 of 21 decision checks held.
limitations: Invented replicas with planted traps, three seeds: what the kind decides, not how well it does on real data.
Checks on one seed share its data, so they are not independent: the interval over seeds is the honest one.
